She can't feel the left side of her body. He's sixty-nine. Together they've driven through all thirty-one provinces and regions of mainland China.
Liu Peijin, from Shandong, married his primary school classmate.
He spent eighteen years in the army, mostly far away from her.
In twenty ten, complications from diabetes left her partly paralysed.
Hospital stays didn't stop her decline. So they made a deal: rather die on the road than in a hospital bed.
In twenty fourteen they set off in an ordinary car.
Later he got a camper van: two beds, a sink, a table, and a cupboard full of medicine.
He calls himself the driver, cook, doctor, nurse and carer, all in one.
Strangers help. In Fujian, villagers come running when their van loses control on a steep road. A hair salon owner won't take their money.
This year in Xinjiang, a tourist films him feeding her. The video spreads across China.
He says life on the road made her a hundred times more spirited.
And they're already planning the next trip.
Would you do this for the person you love?
